key_risks.title: Provisional UK energy book
key_risks.body: Zero register or filing blend on exposure and preparedness — entire profile assessed from public placement pages. Top weighted lines: book concentration 4/4 (600+ clients, 95+ specialists), non-firm intensity 3/4, aggregation/correlation 3/4. Tier label: assessed — close via register_pull on Gallagher-placed UK generator and BESS accounts.

key_risks.title: Grid-geography client stacking
key_risks.body: Alesco RMS concentrates Gallagher's UK Energy, Power & Renewables placement — 600+ accounts through 95+ specialists on shared grid peril and constraint geographies (aggregation 3/4). A single UK low-wind or transmission event can hit multiple cedant programmes Alesco places in the same quarter; broker aggregation is not separately capital-modelled.

key_risks.title: Indemnity-first availability gap
key_risks.body: Mainline placements remain traditional indemnity programmes (trigger gap 2/4). Curtailment and generation shortfall losses on UK wind, solar and BESS clients may not respond under physical-damage BI wordings — Gallagher Specialty's parametric desk partially closes the gap but is not the default Alesco route. Absent trigger: indexed availability / parametric yield cover on standard renewals.

key_risks.title: Provisional BESS pipeline
key_risks.body: No register or filing-backed sub-factors — 0% deterministic blend. Largest assessed lines: book concentration 3/4, non-firm intensity 3/4, tenor mismatch 3/4 on a UK BESS-focused book. Tier label: assessed — close via register_pull on storage asset connection registers and disclosed product wordings.

key_risks.title: BESS operating vs curtailment
key_risks.body: Altelium's all-risk BESS programme and telemetry-led monitoring address battery operating risk and asset performance — not grid-constraint curtailment indexed to NESO boundary events. Non-firm intensity 3/4 reflects interruptible storage assets, but absent trigger type: parametric availability / curtailment BI separate from equipment damage. Disclosed non-damage count is strong; UK grid availability wording still thin.

key_risks.title: UK storage book concentration
key_risks.body: Book concentrates on UK battery-storage operating risk rather than diversified energy intermediation (book concentration 3/4). Growing BESS pipeline stacks on shared constraint geographies — moderate aggregation 2/4 today but rises as Altelium scales. Tier-one monitoring (4/4) outruns register evidence on which sites sit on flexible connections.

key_risks.title: Provisional DC placement stack
key_risks.body: Zero deterministic weight on exposure and preparedness — all sub-factors assessed from Aon's data-centre solutions pages. Top lines: book concentration 4/4, product fit 4/4, capital/access 4/4; non-firm intensity 2/4. Tier label: assessed — close via register_pull on UK DC campus grid connections and cedant SFCR filings.

key_risks.title: Off-site power, no curtailment
key_risks.body: Aon's data-centre practice bundles energy integration and off-site power inside construction and operational property/BI programmes — not dedicated curtailment or availability covers. Grid-dependent campuses face non-firm intensity (2/4) but absent trigger: parametric grid-constraint or indexed availability BI on standard DC placements. Damage-linked DSU/BI remains the default channel despite strong carrier access.

key_risks.title: Placement depth vs monitoring
key_risks.body: Preparedness scores high on specialist teams and carrier relationships (underwriting 4/4, capital 4/4) but data monitoring 3/4 without proprietary UK curtailment telemetry. A large DC book (concentration 4/4) can be placed before connection-register evidence lands — aggregation 2/4 understates clustered South East England campuses on shared boundaries.

key_risks.title: Provisional weather-index book
key_risks.body: No register blend — exposure and preparedness fully assessed. Top weighted lines: non-firm intensity 3/4, aggregation/correlation 3/4, data/pricing 4/4. Trigger gap 0/4 (disclosed non-damage product count). Tier label: assessed on US energy/ag portfolio — close via register_pull if UK cedant participation grows.

key_risks.title: Regional index correlation
key_risks.body: Arbol's weather-indexed energy covers pay on parametric triggers by design (trigger gap 0/4) — but index portfolios correlate across regions when shared weather drivers hit multiple policies (aggregation 3/4). A broad US low-wind or drought episode can trigger concurrent payouts on generation-linked indices; non-firm intensity 3/4 on renewable offtakers amplifies basis risk where index ≠ site-level curtailment.

key_risks.title: UK grid availability absent
key_risks.body: Book concentration 2/4 — US-centric parametric energy MGA with limited direct UK power/DC cedant stack. Strong parametric architecture does not extend to UK NESO constraint-indexed availability products documented on Arbol's energy pages. Product fit 4/4 on weather parametrics vs NFRI-specific curtailment gap if UK expansion proceeds without register-linked indices.

key_risks.title: Provisional index portfolio
key_risks.body: Zero filing/register blend — assessed profile across agriculture, corporate hedging and renewable yield lines. Top lines: data monitoring 4/4, product fit 4/4, parent capital 4/4; non-firm intensity 3/4, aggregation 3/4. Trigger gap 0/4 (disclosed). Tier label: assessed — close via register_pull on UK renewable cedant registers.

key_risks.title: Spatial yield index correlation
key_risks.body: AXA Climate writes index-based renewable yield and corporate climate hedges where non-firm intensity 3/4 and spatial aggregation 3/4 bite together — one low-resource period triggers multiple index covers on wind and solar portfolios. Parametric triggers are core architecture (trigger gap 0/4) but correlated index design concentrates tail risk on parent AXA balance sheet without UK constraint-boundary granularity.

key_risks.title: Group capital, thin UK register
key_risks.body: Parent AXA Group capacity (4/4) supports large index policies, but book concentration 2/4 reflects diversified global lines — UK power/DC cedant stack unverified at asset level. Tenor mismatch 1/4 on multi-year climate structures vs short UK yield history. Absent: ECR/TEC register rows tying index bases to site-level non-firm connections.

key_risks.title: Provisional specialty broker
key_risks.body: Entire profile assessed — 0% deterministic blend, overall confidence low. Top exposure lines: book concentration 2/4, non-firm 2/4, trigger gap 2/4; preparedness thin on data monitoring 1/4 and pricing 1/4. Tier label: assessed — close via register_pull and trigger_mining on UK renewables placements.

key_risks.title: No parametric or telemetry desk
key_risks.body: BMS Group places modest UK renewables and power business with no evidenced parametric desk, proprietary curtailment monitoring or pricing methodology (data 1/4, pricing 1/4, product fit 2/4). Clients on flexible connections face availability losses that standard indemnity BI may not trigger — absent: indexed availability cover and grid telemetry on renewals.

key_risks.title: Sidelined MoS, assessed only
key_risks.body: Margin of safety −5.0 (sidelined) — exposure 45/100 vs preparedness 40/100 on an entirely assessed evidence base. Low aggregation 1/4 limits correlated tail today, but channel neither concentrates differentiated non-firm risk nor closes trigger gaps vs Gallagher or Aon DC practices. No SFCR or register cedant data disclosed.

key_risks.title: Provisional MGU incubator
key_risks.body: All sub-factors assessed — 0% register blend across ~13 Castel units including Renewable Energy, marine and construction. Top lines: trigger gap 3/4, book concentration 2/4, non-firm 2/4; capital 1/4 on Ryan Specialty delegated authority. Tier label: assessed — close via register_pull on renewable unit binders.

key_risks.title: Renewables unit indemnity gap
key_risks.body: Castel's dedicated Renewable Energy unit exposes part of the book to generation and curtailment risk (non-firm 2/4) but products remain indemnity-based with no parametric availability cover (trigger gap 3/4). Absent trigger: indexed yield or grid-constraint BI on BESS and wind accounts. Ryan Specialty acquisition adds scale without closing non-damage wordings on the renewable binder.

key_risks.title: Thin delegated capital stack
key_risks.body: Delegated-authority MGU platform (capital 1/4) relies on third-party/Ryan-affiliated carrier capacity without disclosed AA-tier depth for correlated UK renewable losses. Pricing methodology unpublished (1/4); data monitoring 2/4. A constraint event hitting multiple renewable unit accounts could exhaust per-program limits before group retro responds.

key_risks.title: Provisional diversified MGA
key_risks.body: Zero deterministic blend — assessed across 30+ specialty classes. Direct energy exposure low: book concentration 1/4, non-firm 1/4, aggregation 1/4. Top preparedness line: data monitoring 3/4 via Connect platform. Tier label: assessed — NFRI relevance peripheral to core cyber/tech book.

key_risks.title: Carbon delivery ≠ curtailment
key_risks.body: CFC's carbon non-delivery cover is event/trigger-driven (partial trigger gap closure 2/4) but insures credit delivery failure — not UK grid availability or generation curtailment on power assets. Absent trigger: indexed constraint or parametric availability BI for data-centre and renewable cedants. Product fit 2/4 for NFRI-specific curtailment risk.

key_risks.title: Emerging-risk tenor gap
key_risks.body: Carbon and tech emerging-risk lines carry limited loss history against policy tenors (tenor mismatch 2/4). Digital underwriting tooling (Connect/APIs) supports fast placement but does not substitute for UK constraint-register evidence. Delegated carrier capacity 1/4 — tail on correlated emerging-risk events sits on cedant stacks CFC does not separately model for grid stress.

key_risks.title: Provisional parametric reinsurer
key_risks.body: Assessed profile with one disclosed non-damage product line (trigger gap 3/4). Top exposure line: aggregation/correlation 4/4 — highest in batch. Book concentration 1/4, non-firm 1/4. Tier label: assessed — close via register_pull on cedant portfolio compositions.

key_risks.title: Portfolio parametric correlation
key_risks.body: Demex structures parametric stop-loss and portfolio-level weather hedging — aggregation 4/4 because shared climate indices trigger across multiple cedant portfolios in the same window. Strong data and pricing (4/4) outpace product fit 2/4 for asset-level UK grid availability. A regional weather shock hits Demex's correlated reinsurance layer before individual cedant limits bind.

key_risks.title: Stop-loss vs site curtailment
key_risks.body: Demex's disclosed parametric product count (n=1) covers portfolio stop-loss — not UK asset-level curtailment or NESO constraint-indexed availability. Absent trigger: per-site non-firm BI for UK power and DC cedants. Capital 2/4 on a growing book; tenor mismatch 1/4 on multi-year climate hedges vs thin UK comparable loss history.

key_risks.title: Provisional yield parametric book
key_risks.body: Zero register blend — assessed renewable yield/revenue and NDBI lines with disclosed non-damage product architecture (trigger gap 0/4). Top exposure: book concentration 3/4, non-firm 3/4, aggregation 3/4. Tier label: assessed — close via register_pull on UK wind/solar cedant asset registers.

key_risks.title: Low-wind multi-cover trigger
key_risks.body: Descartes underwrites renewable yield and output shortfall on P50-indexed per-GWh triggers — non-firm intensity 3/4 on interruptible generation. Index covers on wind resource/yield are spatially correlated (aggregation 3/4): one UK low-wind period triggers multiple policies simultaneously. Parametric NDBI closes the physical-damage gap (0/4) but index basis risk remains vs site-level curtailment.

key_risks.title: Multi-year resilience tenor
key_risks.body: Descartes promotes multi-year parametric resilience structures (tenor mismatch 2/4) against relatively thin UK parametric-yield claims history. Tier-one capacity to $200m per policy (Munich Re, Swiss Re CS, AXA Climate) absorbs individual losses, but stacked multi-year yield covers on correlated indices extend tail beyond short experience window. Honest tier: assessed on tenor sub-factor.

key_risks.title: Provisional flood parametric MGA
key_risks.body: Fully assessed profile — 0% deterministic blend. Book concentration 1/4, non-firm 1/4; aggregation 3/4 on flood peril. One disclosed non-damage product (trigger gap 3/4 on NFRI scale). Tier label: assessed — peripheral to UK power/DC curtailment index.

key_risks.title: Flood peril, not grid NFRI
key_risks.body: FloodFlash uses sensor-verified depth triggers for commercial flood BI — strong parametric monitoring 4/4 but product fit 2/4 for NFRI curtailment risk. Non-firm intensity 1/4: book unrelated to power generation or data-centre grid availability. Absent: constraint-indexed availability or curtailment BI for UK energy cedants — flood parametric architecture does not transfer to grid stress.

key_risks.title: Regional flood event clustering
key_risks.body: Aggregation/correlation 3/4 — a major UK flood event triggers multiple sensor-linked policies in the same catchment simultaneously. NormanMax-backed capacity (3/4) supports individual limits, but correlated flood depth triggers concentrate tail on geographic clusters unlike diversified peril books. No UK power cedant register linkage documented.

key_risks.title: Provisional DC intermediary stack
key_risks.body: Zero register/filing blend — assessed from Gallagher data-centre solutions pages. Top lines: book concentration 3/4, product fit 3/4, trigger gap 1/4; non-firm 2/4. Tier label: assessed — close via register_pull on UK DC campus connections and Alesco energy cedant registers.

key_risks.title: Damage-linked DC BI default
key_risks.body: Gallagher's digital-infrastructure practice addresses construction, property and operational covers on grid-dependent campuses — placements centre on damage-linked BI rather than curtailment availability (trigger gap 1/4). Absent trigger: parametric grid-constraint or indexed availability cover on standard DC renewals. Alesco RMS energy book under the same group stacks additional generation risk without unified parametric routing.

key_risks.title: Specialist access, thin telemetry
key_risks.body: Moderate preparedness — specialist teams and market access (underwriting 3/4, capital 3/4) without proprietary parametric products or curtailment telemetry (data monitoring 2/4). Parent-group scale places meaningful DC and energy business before UK connection-register evidence lands. Aggregation 2/4 may understate clustered campuses on shared constraint boundaries.
